```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
options(digits=2)
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
require(lubridate)
kRdata <- read.csv(file = 'kRdata.csv')
kRdata <- kRdata %>%
mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
kData = kRdata
```
Data are from the Patient_Info dataset from South Korea 1 Jan to 1 May 2020. These data were retrieved from a downloadable zip file from kaggle.

Some of the data were uncoded for sex - sex must be just male or female.  77 of the data entries were coded sex as blank, so we omit these.  State of a patient must be died or alive - we adjust that as well.  This is done in the mutate function. 

Variables of interest: sex, result

Research Question: - Is dying independent of sex?

# Introduction

Using KData, can we determine that men and women are equally likely to die of covid19 from data collected in South Korea through May 2019?

$H_0$ There is a relationship between gender and death from covid19 in South Korea in 2019.   

$H_0$ There is no relationship between gender and death form covid19 in South Korea in 2019.  

#Methods 

Sex is categorical  
Result is categorical 

# Data Results

## Graphical results    

```{r}
barchartGC(~result + sex,data=kData)
barchartGC(~result + sex,data=kData, type="percent")

```

The graph suggests that makes are likely to die in comparison to females. 

## Numerical results

```{r}
table1 <- xtabs(~result + Sex, data=kData)
rowPerc(table1)
colPerc(table1)
```
The numerical result shows that out of 100, 64% of makes dead compared to 36% of females, indicating that men are afraid twice as likely to die than women.  

## Inferential results 

```{r}
chisq.test(table1)
chisqtestGC(table1)
fisher.test(table1)
```

The p value is 0.001, which is less than 0.05. This means that we reject the null hypotheses. We conclude that there is a connection between sex and death from covid19.  

# Conclusions

To answer the question, can we determine that men and women are equally likely to die of covid19 from data collected in South korea through May 2019? 

We reject the null hypothesis and conclude that there is a relationship between sex and death from covid19. That graphical summary shows that men have an increased likelihood of death compared to women. Furthermore the costs ratio says that men die of 2.3 times the rate of women from covid19.
